0: Knights by Minoru Murao (DMP) is a dark medieval fantasy adventure. In a land where the church burns suspected witches, the masked squire Mist, feared and hated by villagers as the Black Knight, works against the Saints behind the witch hunts. He travels with Euphemia, a young girl with a gift for brewing potions and poisons. It's a moody, action-driven read for fans of sword-and-sorcery with a grim edge.
2: Märchen by Hayate Kuku (Seven Seas) is a fantasy Boys' Love story built around a magical contract. An enchanted coat seals Sakim, the Divine Beast of the Moon, inside its magic circle, and when the summoner Gil inherits it, he gains command of Sakim. The pair set off together through wolf-filled forests, haunted towns, and bogs of the dead. It suits readers who like their romance wrapped in a dark fairy-tale journey.
3: Magika: Swordsman and Summoner by Mitsuki Mihara (Seven Seas) is a magic-school fantasy with plenty of action and comedy. Humanity has learned to call mythical beings from a parallel dimension, and fifteen-year-old Kazuki Hayashizaki becomes the first male summoner ever, enrolling at a school that has only ever admitted women. His sister, a magic swordswoman sworn to protect summoners, is dead set against it. It's a fit for fans of harem-flavored academy fantasy.
4: Cheeky Brat by Miyuki Mitsubachi (Yen Press) is a sweet, funny high school romance. Yuki Machida, the cool-headed manager of the basketball team, has spent years helping raise her five younger siblings and keeps her own feelings tucked away. She has a crush on the team captain, but a teasing underclassman, Sho Naruse, won't stop pursuing her. It's a warm pick for readers who love push-and-pull romances with a grounded heroine.
5: Dragon Hunter by Hong Seock Seo (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy action series steeped in folklore. In an ancient Korea terrorized by dragons, money-hungry hunter Seur Chong takes on the beasts with help from shamans, all while trying to live up to the legend of the great hunter Andrew Yi. Afflicted by the Dragon's Curse, he has to slay a blue dragon if he wants to survive. Expect brawling monster fights, roguish humor, and a mythic backdrop.
6: Dance in the Vampire Bund: Age of Scarlet Order by Nozomu Tamaki (Seven Seas) is a dark supernatural sequel to the original vampire saga. In a United States gripped by vampire hunts, rumors spread that Mina Tepes will gather American vampires on the West Coast and carry them by ship to the Vampire Bund. But the Bund sank months ago, and Mina is said to be dead. It's for readers who want more gothic intrigue and action from the Bund's world.
7: Free Life Fantasy Online: Immortal Princess by Akisuzu Nenohi (Seven Seas) is a relaxed, funny VRMMO fantasy light novel. Gamer Kotone Tsukishiro gets a copy of Free Life Fantasy Online from her younger sister and picks one of its hardest inhuman races to play: a zombie. Her very first quest pulls her into a world that soon becomes a big part of her real life. It's a cozy pick for readers who enjoy game-world stories with an offbeat hero.
8: Phantom Busters by Neoshoco (Viz Media) is a lively supernatural comedy set at a high school. Top student Eugene Korekishi doesn't believe in ghosts, but his classmate Mogari Shishikuro is an exorcist who eats them. Since Mogari can't actually see ghosts himself, the two need someone with the sight, so they start a school exorcist club. It's a fun fit for fans of spooky buddy comedies with plenty of energy.
10: Yakuza Reincarnation by Takeshi Natsuhara and Hiroki Miyashita (Seven Seas) is a rowdy isekai action series with a tough-guy heart. An old-school yakuza is killed by young thugs while defending his turf and wakes up in a fantasy world as a young princess, Sanaria Ryu Lundberg, with his tattoo and strength intact. Now he may be the only one who can teach this world what yakuza honor means. It's great for readers who like brawls, gruff humor, and a fish-out-of-water lead.
12: Pastel by Toshihiko Kobayashi (Del Rey) is a gentle, comedic teen romance. After getting dumped, high schooler Mugi Mugimaru meets Yuu Tsukishima during a summer away and falls for her hard, only to find that she ends up living under the same roof as him. Their awkward closeness sets up plenty of misunderstandings and sweet moments. It's a good pick for fans of classic slice-of-life love stories with a soft, summery feel.
14: The World After the Fall by singNsong and Undead Gamja (Ize Press) is a big, brooding action fantasy adapted from the Korean web novel. Enormous towers appear around the world, swarms of monsters follow, and humanity's survival comes to rest on the Tower Walkers tasked with climbing to the top. Jaehwan begins to suspect the mission isn't what it seems and resolves to trust only himself on the way to Floor 100. It's for readers who like sprawling, philosophical battle stories with a lone-wolf hero.
16: Pokémon: Sword & Shield by Hidenori Kusaka and Satoshi Yamamoto (Viz Media) is a bright, kid-friendly adventure based on the Galar region video games. Casey Shield, a hacker who invented the Dynamax Simulator, wants to reunite with a lost Pokémon. Henry Sword, who repairs gear for Pokémon, is searching for the Rusted Sword and Rusted Shield. It's a great pick for young fans of the games and longtime Pokémon Adventures readers.
18: The Strange Adventure of a Broke Mercenary by Mine (Seven Seas) is a grounded sword-and-sorcery light novel. After the mercenaries who raised him die in a bloody battle, Loren is left with only his wits and his sword, so he turns to adventuring. His reckless new party treats him as a meat shield, and only their priest, Lapis, sees what he's worth. It's for readers who like a gruff, practical hero and a partnership that builds over time.
19: Angel Diary by Lee YunHee and Kara (Ice Kunion) is a lighthearted Korean fantasy romance. Dong-Hwa, a princess of Heaven, runs away to Earth to escape an arranged marriage to the King of Demons and hides out disguised as a high school boy. It isn't long before guardians from Heaven and the demon world come looking for her. It's a fun pick for fans of gender-bender comedy, lovely art, and celestial romance.
20: The Queen's Knight by Kim Kang-Won (Tokyopop) is a Korean portal fantasy with a romantic heart. As a girl, Yuna is rescued by a mysterious knight named Rieno, who swears to protect her. Years later she's drawn into his world, Phantasmagoria, where she's expected to take her place as its queen. It's for readers who like a fish-out-of-water heroine, a devoted protector, and plenty of court drama.
21: Crossplay Love: Otaku x Punk by Toru (Seven Seas) is a playful romantic comedy built on mistaken identities. Gloomy student Yuuma Hanae secretly works at a maid café as "Hana," and his delinquent schoolmate Shuumei Satogiri falls for Hana without knowing who she really is. Shuumei starts visiting the café dressed as a girl named Mei, and soon each is crushing on someone they think is a woman. It's a sweet, silly pick for fans of crossdressing comedies.
23: Into the Deepest, Most Unknowable Dungeon by Kakeru (Seven Seas) is an isekai fantasy adventure with a harem streak. After being hit by a truck, a former temp worker is reborn in another world as Jean, an average boy with no special abilities. Armed only with the practical know-how from his past life, he sets out to conquer the deepest, most mysterious dungeon in this new world. It's a fit for readers who like underdog heroes and dungeon crawling.
25: Mint Chocolate by Mami Orikasa (Yen Press) is a sweet and bittersweet high school romance. Nanami's longtime crush, suddenly becomes her stepbrother when their parents marry, and now she has to live with him under the same roof. His cold, arrogant attitude doesn't make things any easier. It's a cozy pick for fans of step-sibling romances and slow-thawing love interests.
26: Backstabbed in a Backwater Dungeon by Shisui Meikyou and Takafumi Oomae (Seven Seas) is a revenge-driven fantasy action series. Light is betrayed and left for dead by his adventuring party deep in a dungeon, but there he awakens an Infinite Gacha ability that summons allies at level 9999. With a loyal army at his back, he sets out to pay back everyone who wronged him. It's for readers who enjoy overpowered heroes and dark, satisfying payback stories.
27: His Majesty the Demon King's Housekeeper by Saiko Wadori and Mika Kajiyama (Seven Seas) is a charming isekai fantasy with a romantic thread. High schooler Sakura Takatsuki loves cleaning, so when she's swept into another world and lands in a realm ruled by a Demon King, she can't stand the grime. A witch's curse has blocked all cleaning magic there, so Sakura rolls up her sleeves and sets out to scrub the place clean herself. It's a gentle, upbeat read for fans of cozy fantasy.
29: iD_eNTITY by Hee-Joon Son and Youn-Kyung Kim (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy action series set inside an online game. Every night, Roto plays a virtual-reality game with two friends, and together they make a warrior, sorcerer, and healer team. Their in-game reputation has grown big enough to cause trouble for them, both inside the game and out. It's a fun read for gamers and fans of MMO adventures with a comedic edge.
30: Boys Be by Masahiro Itabashi (Tokyopop) is a sweet and comedic collection of teen romance stories. Each chapter follows a different high school boy as he works up the nerve to confess, stumbles through a first date, or wonders whether a girl he likes feels the same way. The stories are short, earnest, and often funny about the awkwardness of growing up. It's a nostalgic, easygoing read for fans of anthology-style love stories.
31: The Young Magician by Yuri Narushima (CMX) is a dark fantasy with an occult bent. Carno Guino is a magician whose soul is fused with demons, and Ibuki Shikishima is a Shinto practitioner, and the two young men are drawn into a tangled war between rival magical factions. Expect moody atmosphere, elegant art, and a slow-building partnership. It's a good fit for readers who like supernatural drama with plenty of mystery.
32: Species Domain by Shunsuke Noro (Seven Seas) is a gentle fantasy comedy set in a high school where elves, dwarves, and angels study alongside humans. Kazamori is an elf girl raised by humans who can't actually use magic, though everyone assumes she can. Her classmate Ohki, meanwhile, insists magic doesn't exist and everything can be explained by science. It's a funny, good-natured read for fans of slice-of-life school stories with a fantasy twist.
34: The Eccentric Doctor of the Moon Flower Kingdom by Tohru Himuka (Seven Seas) is a historical fantasy that mixes medical drama with romance. In the Moon Flower Kingdom, healing has long relied on superstition, and Prince Keiun is looking for something better. When his party is attacked, he watches an unusual teenage girl named Koyou perform a lifesaving procedure. It's for readers who enjoy clever heroines, court intrigue, and stories in the spirit of The Apothecary Diaries.
35: My Special One by Momoko Koda (Viz Media) is a sweet and funny shojo romance. After a humiliating rejection, Sahoko Wakaume swears she'll never fall for a good-looking guy again. So when idol Kouta Kirigaya starts showing up at her family's restaurant, she gives him the cold shoulder, even as she slowly begins to warm up to him. It's a light, heartfelt pick for fans of celebrity romances and down-to-earth heroines.
37: Phantom Tales of the Night by Matsuri (Yen Press) is a dark supernatural fantasy with a mysterious edge. The Murakumo Inn serves both humans and non-humans, and instead of payment, its enigmatic owner asks each guest for a deeply shameful secret. High schooler Tokihito Sasaki learns he has been dead for a long time and was revived by the owner as a living corpse. Fans of xxxHolic and Hell Girl will enjoy its eerie, elegant mood.
38: Today's Cerberus by Ato Sakurai (Yen Press) is a supernatural comedy with a harem twist. As a child, Chiaki Mikado was bitten by a three-headed dog, and he has been listless ever since. Then his father sends him Kuro from Greece, who says she's there to protect him; she turns out to be one of three girls who together make up Cerberus, and they move in with Chiaki to make amends. It's light, silly fun for fans of mythological romcoms.
39: Kamui by Shingo Nanami (Broccoli Books) is a sweeping shonen action fantasy. When the sacred spirit Okikurumi is stolen from Atsuma's village, the kamui spirits fall into chaos and the world itself is threatened. Atsuma, carrying the spirit of an ancient sword, leaves home to get it back and joins NOA, a group of youths who wield kamui power. It's a good pick for fans of spirit-powered battles and quest stories.
40: Snow Drop by Choi Kyung-ah (Tokyopop) is a heartfelt Korean romance with a dramatic streak. After a painful past, Yoo So-na finds comfort in tending the flowers at her family's nursery. Back at high school, she meets Oh Hae-gi, a teen model, and the two bond over the hurts they both carry, even as their families push back against the relationship. It's a good pick for readers who love emotional, melodramatic first-love stories.
41: Kamen Rider Kuuga by Toshiki Inoue and Hitotsu Yokoshima (Titan Manga) is a grown-up reimagining of the classic tokusatsu hero. When the ancient Grongi tribe awakens and begins killing people in modern Japan, a cheerful wanderer named Yusuke Godai finds a mysterious belt that transforms him into the warrior Kuuga. Working alongside detective Kaoru Ichijo, he takes on the monsters one battle at a time. It's a strong pick for longtime Rider fans and newcomers who like gritty hero action.
43: Succubus and Hitman by Makoto Fukami and Seigo Tokiya (Seven Seas) is a dark supernatural revenge story. High schooler Gamou Shouya is, in a sense, already dead: his body now holds the soul of a boy who made a pact with the succubus Armelina. He works as her hitman, and in return she helps him hunt down the people who murdered him and his family. It's for readers who like grim, stylish action with a demonic partnership at its core.
45: Gacha Gacha by Hiroyuki Tamakoshi (Del Rey) is a lively romantic comedy with a gaming twist. Kouhei has long had a crush on his sweet, studious classmate Kurara, but an encounter with a video game leaves her with several different personalities that pop out without warning. Kouhei ends up keeping her secret and trying to manage the chaos. It's a breezy read for fans of romcoms full of mix-ups and misunderstandings.
46: Monster Guild: The Dark Lord's (No-Good) Comeback! by Tourou (Seven Seas) is a goofy fantasy comedy told from the villain's side. After being defeated by a hero who just won't stay dead, the once all-powerful Dark Lord survives only by splitting off a sliver of his soul, leaving him weaker than a slime. To reclaim his throne, he starts building a guild of monsters from the ground up. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy fantasy parodies and underdog villains.
47: Am I Actually the Strongest? by Sai Sumimori and Ai Takahashi (Kodansha) is a lighthearted isekai fantasy comedy. Reborn as Haruto, a baby prince in a world of magic, the hero is judged to have no magical talent and is cast out of the royal family. In truth he's absurdly powerful, and he would much rather live a quiet life than let anyone find out. It's an easygoing pick for fans of overpowered heroes and gentle, comic adventures.
48: Nora: The Last Chronicle of Devildom by Kazunari Kakei (Viz Media) is a high-energy supernatural action comedy. Nora is a delinquent demon whose true form is Cerberus, a vicious hound of disaster, but he can only use his magic with permission from Kazuma, a human student who is very reluctant to give it. The Dark Liege wants the mismatched pair to team up against renegade demons in the human world. It's a fun read for fans of bickering-partner battle manga.
49: Beauty and the Feast by Satomi U (Square Enix Manga) is a warm, food-centered romantic comedy. Shuuko Yakumo, a 28-year-old widow, has been drifting through life until Shohei Yamato, a 15-year-old high school baseball recruit, moves in next door. Noticing that he lives on convenience store food and has an enormous appetite, she starts cooking him dinner, and her love of cooking slowly returns. It's a cozy, gentle pick for fans of slice-of-life stories built around home-cooked meals.
50: One by Lee Vin (Tokyopop) is a Korean music-industry drama with a romantic thread. In public, high schooler Jenny You is a pop princess, but in private she's a rebellious beauty her classmates shun. Her quiet classmate Eumpa Won, nicknamed "One," gave up his childhood fame as a musical prodigy in the United States to live an ordinary life, until his music teacher steals his work and passes it off as his own. It's for readers who love stories about talent, fame, and first love.
51: Black Night Parade by Hikaru Nakamura (Seven Seas) is an offbeat supernatural comedy with a dark streak. Hino Miharu works a dead-end convenience store job and spends Christmas alone, until a run-in with a shadowy Black Santa, the one who deals with bad children, gets him whisked off to the Arctic. There he's hired into a sprawling Christmas operation that may be a dream job or a nightmare. It's for readers who like cynical, quirky humor and a holiday story with a twist.
52: Blade of Heaven by Yong-su Hwang and Kyung-il Yang (Tokyopop) is a Korean martial arts fantasy full of action and humor, drawn from Asian myth and legend. Young Soma is accused by the King of Heaven of stealing his sword, and he sets out with Princess Aroomee and General Winter to track down the legendary Blade of Heaven. It's a fun pick for fans of energetic sword fights and mythic adventures.
53: Blazin' Barrels by Min-Seo Park (Tokyopop) is a Korean action comedy set in a futuristic Wild West. Sting looks harmless and naive, but he's a skilled fighter with dreams of becoming a bounty hunter. When he spots a bounty for Gold Romany, an all-girl gang of outlaws, he figures capturing them is his ticket to fame and fortune. It's a rowdy, good-humored read for fans of gunslinger adventures and goofy heroes.
56: Jack Frost by JinHo Ko (Yen Press) is a Korean supernatural action series with a horror edge. Noh-A Joo is a new student at Amityville High School, and she quickly learns the school is not what it seems. She's pulled into a war between vampires, monsters, and other creatures, and has to figure out her role as a "mirror image" while dealing with the mysterious Jack Frost. It's for readers who like bloody, stylish battles and dark mysteries.
57: Karate Survivor in Another World by Yazin and Takahito Kobayashi (Seven Seas) is a scrappy isekai survival adventure. A martial artist is reborn in a fantasy world after a clumsy deity drops him deep in a wild forest. With no magic and no cheat skills, he has nothing to rely on but his wits and his karate. It's a fun change of pace for readers who like grounded, hand-to-hand action and a hero who earns every win the hard way.
58: Ragnarok by Lee Myung-Jin (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy adventure rooted in Norse mythology. Chaos is an amnesiac warrior living in the village of Fayon, while the fierce Fenris searches for the reincarnation of the god Balder in order to bring about Ragnarok. What follows is a sweeping tale full of swordplay, gods, and monsters. It's a natural pick for fans of the Ragnarok Online game and anyone who likes old-school high-fantasy action.
59: Knight of the Ice by Yayoi Ogawa (Kodansha) is a funny, warmhearted romance set in the world of figure skating. Kokoro Kijinami is an internationally celebrated skater famous for his elegant, knightly performances, but off the ice he's a hopeless romantic and an anime fan. He can only land his quad jumps when his childhood friend Chitose is nearby to recite a spell from a magical girl show. It's a delight for fans of sports romance and quirky couples.
60: Yokai Cats by Pandania (Seven Seas) is a playful, full-color comedy about pet cats with a secret. These seemingly ordinary house cats are actually supernatural yokai who can stretch their necks to swipe food off the counter or turn into a giant wall to block your path. The series turns everyday cat mischief into folklore-flavored fun. It's a family-friendly pick for cat lovers of all ages.
63: Zo Zo Zombie by Yasunari Nagatoshi (JY) is a silly, kid-friendly horror comedy. Fifth grader Isamu goes looking for the zombie rumored to haunt a playground and finds Zombie Boy asleep in the sandbox. Zombie Boy can swap his blood for tomato juice and pop his limbs off and on, and he'd much rather be friends than eat brains, though his weird antics keep landing Isamu in trouble. It's a great fit for young readers who love gross-out gags and slapstick.
64: Enchanter by Izumi Kawachi (DMP) is a supernatural romantic comedy. In a world where enchanters craft magical items using power from contracted demons, high schooler Haruhiko Kanou is approached by the demon Eukanaria, who wants to revive her lost love, the enchanter Fulcanelli, by placing his soul in Haruhiko's body. Haruhiko, meanwhile, has a secret crush on his childhood friend Yuka. It's a lighthearted pick for fans of love triangles with a magical twist.
65: Sorry for My Familiar by Tekka Yaguraba (Seven Seas) is a goofy fantasy comedy about a mismatched pair of travelers. A young demon girl ends up with a familiar who is anything but ordinary: an eccentric older man and mad monster researcher whose obsession with creatures makes him a handful. The two set out on the road together, and his enthusiasm keeps dragging them into trouble. It's a fun read for fans of offbeat fantasy humor and odd-couple adventures.
66: Spirits and Cat Ears by Miyuki Nakayama (Yen Press) is a cozy supernatural comedy with a romantic heart. Neneko Izuna, a young but experienced shrine maiden, and her shikigami partner, Sagami Shichikage, move to the Waka Clinic to help exorcise evil spirits. The story follows their everyday lives and spirit-busting jobs as a gentle romance grows between them. It's a sweet pick for readers who like cat-eared spirits, folklore, and slice-of-life charm.
67: Anyway, I'm Falling in Love with You. by Haruka Mitsui (Kodansha) is a heartfelt shojo romance about childhood friends on the edge of growing up. Mizuho dreams of watching the summer fireworks with the right person, and several boys are drawn to her, including her childhood friend Kizuki and the brainy future doctor Shin. All the while, she worries that growing up will pull her and her friends apart. It's a lovely pick for fans of love triangles and bittersweet youth.
68: Steel of the Celestial Shadows by Daruma Matsuura (Viz Media) is a strange and inventive samurai adventure. Konosuke is a samurai cursed so that metal repels him, leaving him unable to wield a sword. Despairing, he resolves to die, but a woman saves him and, to his surprise, proposes marriage. It's for readers who enjoy historical action with a supernatural twist, offbeat humor, and an unusual couple at its center.
70: Futaribeya: A Room for Two by Yukiko (Tokyopop) is a gentle yuri slice-of-life story. Responsible Sakurako Kawawa is about to start high school and moves into a school boarding house, where she's paired with roommate Kasumi Yamabuki, an easygoing girl who puts minimal effort into just about everything. Despite their opposite personalities, the two slowly grow close. It's a soft, cozy read for fans of quiet roommate stories and sweet, low-key romance.
71: Monster Hunter: Flash Hunter by Keiichi Hikami and Shin Yamamoto (Viz Media) is a fast-paced action fantasy based on Capcom's hit game series. In a world ruled by monsters, humanity depends on elite hunters for protection. Raiga and his friends are hunters too, but early on they're still inexperienced, and their first clash with a dragon-like monster shows them that poor teamwork could get them killed. It's a great pick for fans of the games and big monster battles.
72: The Dragon Knight's Beloved by Asagi Orikawa and Ritsu Aozaki (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy romance with plenty of dragons. On her sixteenth birthday, Melissa takes a job as a maid at the royal castle to be closer to the dragons and to her idol, Dragon Knight Captain Hubert. When she learns he's about to retire, she fears she's missed her chance, and then he asks her to be his pretend girlfriend. It's a cozy pick for fans of fake-dating romances.
73: Neck and Neck by Lee Sun-Hee (Tokyopop) is a Korean high school romance with a crime-family twist. Dabin Choi is the daughter of Seoul's most powerful crime boss, and she has a crush on Eugene, the son of one of her father's associates, who only sees her as a little sister. When a new classmate turns out to be the son of her father's longtime rival, school becomes a battleground of power games. It's a fun pick for fans of feisty heroines and dramatic love triangles.
74: He's My Only Vampire by Aya Shouoto (Yen Press) is a dark, romantic supernatural drama. Kana was once a gifted long jumper until a leg injury ended her athletic future, and her former teammates now accuse her of faking her pain. When she's badly hurt saving a little girl from a traffic accident, a boy she played with as a child reappears, reveals he's a vampire, and binds her to him to save her life. It's for readers who like brooding paranormal romance with a gothic mood.
75: Not Lives by Wataru Karasuma (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi action series set around a deadly game. Mikami Shigeru is a gamer and aspiring game designer who dreams of creating the ultimate gaming experience. When he finds a mysterious disc among some research materials, it implants itself in his body, and he begins seeing the world through his cool-headed game avatar, Kyouka. Now the two have to survive a game with real-world consequences. It's for fans of high-stakes game-world thrillers.
77: PhD: Phantasy Degree by Hee-Joon Son (Tokyopop) is a lively Korean fantasy comedy. Sang is a spunky girl searching for the Demon School Hades, a place no ordinary human is supposed to set foot in. Once she finds her way in, she falls in with a band of misfit monsters and gets swept up in the hunt for the mysterious Satan's Rings. It's a fun pick for fans of monster-school mischief, slapstick humor, and energetic art.
78: Pieces of a Spiral by Kaimu Tachibana (CMX) is a supernatural action fantasy steeped in reincarnation and old loyalties. Sakuya and Wakyo are reunited in a new life, only to learn that Bishu, their former master, is in danger from demons seeking revenge. They have to protect him before those dark forces take hold of his new life. It's a good pick for readers who like moody demon-hunting stories, devoted partnerships, and elegant shojo-style art.
79: Tokyo Aliens by Naoe (Square Enix) is a stylish sci-fi action series with a mystery at its core. Akira Gunji is an ordinary first-year high school student who hopes to follow his late father into the police force. After witnessing a fight between two people with strange powers on a train, he's abducted by an alien and learns some unsettling truths about his father. It's a fun read for fans of superpowered action and alien conspiracies.
80: Wild Act by Rie Takada (Tokyopop) is a bubbly shojo romance set in the world of acting. Fifteen-year-old Yuniko Sakuraba is so devoted to the late actor Akira Nanae that she'll go to wild lengths to collect his belongings. Her obsession brings her face to face with Ryu Eba, a hot young actor and rival in more ways than one. It's a fun, fast-paced pick for fans of showbiz romance and feisty heroines.
81: Sand Chronicles by Hinako Ashihara (Viz Media) is a moving shojo coming-of-age drama. After her parents divorce, twelve-year-old Ann Uekusa moves with her mother from Tokyo to her mother's hometown in rural Shimane. There she meets Daigo, a local boy, and siblings Fuji and Shika, and the story follows their friendships and first loves as they grow up. It's a beautiful, emotional pick for readers who love character-driven stories that span years.
82: Seimaden by You Higuri (CMX) is a lush gothic fantasy romance. The demon prince Laures loves Hilda, a human dancer who is the reincarnation of his former lover, Ellis, for whom he once gave up his humanity. Hilda knows nothing of her past and finds herself torn between Laures and Roderique, while Laures' loyal deputy schemes to drag him back to the demon world. It's for readers who love dramatic, beautifully drawn tales of forbidden love.
83: Love and Heart by Chitose Kaidou (Yen Press) is a quirky shojo romance with a mysterious edge. After catching her boyfriend cheating, Yoh breaks up with him and wants nothing to do with love. Then Haruma Hirose, a boy from across the street, turns up inside her house with a key her mother gave him, and Yoh starts to suspect he might be a stalker. It's a fun pick for readers who like offbeat romcoms with a slightly eerie love interest.
84: Dragon Voice by Yuriko Nishiyama (Tokyopop) is an upbeat comedy-drama about chasing a dream in the music world. Rin Amami has always loved to sing, but his unusual, gravelly voice gets him laughed at. His big break comes when a boy band takes notice of him. It's a fun pick for readers who like underdog stories, idol-industry drama, and big dreams.
85: Et Cetera by Tow Nakazaki (Tokyopop) is a rollicking action adventure set in an alternate American West. Mingchao, an orphaned girl from China, inherits the Eto gun, which fires bullets powered by the essences of the Chinese zodiac animals. She sets off across the country with a priest named Baskerville to uncover the gun's dark origins, while a crime syndicate hunts the weapon. It's a great pick for fans of gunslinging Westerns with a fantasy twist.
86: Silver Diamond by Shiho Sugiura (Tokyopop) is a gentle fantasy adventure with a warm heart. Rakan Akatsuki is an orphaned boy with a rare gift for making plants grow. One day a mysterious young man named Chigusa appears in his garden from another world, and Rakan's quiet life gives way to dangers and new allies. It's a good fit for readers who like soft, character-driven fantasy and found-family bonds.
87: So What's Wrong with Getting Reborn as a Goblin? by Nazuna Miki and Tsukasa Araki (Yen Press) is a cheerful isekai fantasy comedy. Salaryman Akira Yagami dies saving a boy from a truck and is reborn as a goblin in another world. Goblins usually live only about seven days, but somehow he's inherited an unusually long lifespan, and he sets out to make the most of it. It's an easygoing read for fans of monster-reincarnation stories with a light touch.
89: Of the Red, the Light, and the Ayakashi by HaccaWorks* and Nanao (Yen Press) is an atmospheric supernatural mystery based on a visual novel. Yue has been raised in a Shinto shrine on a mountain and is forbidden to leave or see the outside world. When he visits the town's winter festival with his childhood friend, the black fox Kurogitsune, almost everyone looks like a shadow to him, except for two mysterious boys. It's for readers who like eerie folklore and puzzle-box storytelling.
90: Smokin' Parade by Jinsei Kataoka and Kazuma Kondou (Yen Press) is a gory, high-octane action horror series from the creators of Deadman Wonderland. The Amenotori company has developed technology that can transplant any body part, and Youkou Kakujou's formerly wheelchair-bound sister is one of its success stories. Meanwhile, the area is plagued by grisly killings tied to people in animal-head costumes, and the siblings are pulled into the violence alongside a cyborg team called the Jackolopes. It's for readers with a strong stomach.
91: Love and Heart by Chitose Kaidou (Yen Press) is a quirky shojo romance with a mysterious edge. After catching her boyfriend cheating, Yoh breaks up with him and wants nothing to do with love. Then Haruma Hirose, a boy from across the street, turns up inside her house with a key her mother gave him, and Yoh starts to suspect he might be a stalker. It's a fun pick for readers who like offbeat romcoms with a slightly eerie love interest.
93: After God by Sumi Eno (Viz Media) is a haunting supernatural action story set in a ravaged Japan. Gods have invaded the country, leaving death and destruction behind and turning whole cities into uninhabitable danger zones. Anti-God researcher Sachiyuki Tokinaga is determined to find a way to defeat them, and his path soon crosses with high schooler Waka Kamikura. It's for readers who like eerie, beautifully drawn stories built around one big question: how do you kill a god?
94: Pass the Monster Meat, Milady! by Sakae Esuno (Kodansha) is a cheerful fantasy romcom with a big appetite. Noble lady Melphiera has a secret passion for monsters, and especially for cooking and eating them. When her engagement falls through, she accepts a proposal from the feared "Bloody Duke" Aldo, whose lands happen to be teeming with monsters. It's a delightful pick for fans of foodie fantasy and offbeat, sweet couples.
95: Tune In to the Midnight Heart by Masakuni Igarashi (Kodansha) is an upbeat romantic comedy. Years ago, Arisu Yamabuki was comforted by the livestreams of a mysterious girl called Apollo, and he's never forgotten her voice. After tracing her to a particular high school, he transfers there and discovers she must be one of the four girls in the broadcasting club, so he sets out to find out which one while helping each of them chase her dreams. It's a fun pick for fans of harem romcoms.
96: Nue's Exorcist by Kota Kawae (Viz Media) is a punchy supernatural action series. Gakuro Yakushiji is a timid boy who has been bullied for years, until he stumbles on a mysterious shrine and unseals Nue, a powerful and arrogant yokai. Bound together, the two take on the demons hiding in the human world. It's a fun pick for fans of exorcist battles, monster partners, and underdog heroes.
97: A Tale of the Secret Saint ZERO by Touya and Chibi (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted fantasy prequel light novel. Three hundred years before Fia's adventures, Princess Serafina lives hidden away in a forest with the forest spirits and her cousin, the young knight captain Sirius Ulysses. When an incident awakens mysterious powers inside her, she takes her first steps on the path to becoming the Great Saint. It's a treat for fans of the main series who want to see where the legend began.
98: My Kitten is a Picky Eater by Migiri Miki (Seven Seas) is a gentle, heartwarming slice-of-life comedy. A kind young man named Taiyo Mano rescues a kitten from the snow and names her Yuki. As a first-time pet owner, he quickly discovers that Yuki turns up her nose at store-bought cat food, so he teaches himself to cook to make meals she'll actually eat. It's a cozy pick for cat lovers and fans of comforting food stories.
99: Game of Familia by Mikoto Yamaguchi and D.P (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy adventure built around a blended family. Shy high schooler Sasae Hatsushima feels ordinary next to his accomplished stepfamily, and after his father dies just months into the remarriage, Sasae is pulled into another world with his stepmother Kanae and stepsisters Manako and Hinana. There they're asked to defeat an army of the undead. It's for readers who like isekai with real stakes and family drama.
101: MoMo -the blood taker- by Akira Sugito (Seven Seas) is a dark supernatural mystery with a thread of romance running through it. Tokyo is gripped by a string of murders in which the victims are drained of blood, and rumors of vampires are spreading. Detective Keigo Mikogami is hunting the killer he calls "The Man With Two Faces" to avenge his murdered lover, and his search draws the attention of a mysterious silver-haired girl. It's a good fit for readers who like moody vampire stories with a detective's edge.
102: A-DO by Jaku Amano (Kodansha) is a sci-fi action story with a streetwise heart. In a near-future Japan tense with anti-immigrant protests, Riko, a restless young woman who can't hold down a job, saves a boy named Eito from a speeding truck and ends up looking after him. When an army sniper takes a shot at Eito, plant-like tendrils burst from his arm to stop the bullet. It's a fresh pick for readers who like unlikely guardians and mysterious kids with strange powers.
103: Tank Chair by Manabu Yashiro (Kodansha) is a gritty, high-energy action story. On Guicheng Island, known as the most dangerous town in the universe, gangs fight for power with genetic doping. Young Shizuka takes on risky assassination jobs, but it's her brother Nagi who does the fighting: he took a bullet to protect her and now lies comatose in a heavily armed wheelchair, yet he still carries out every job. It's a great pick for fans of over-the-top battles and fierce sibling bonds.
104: Gazing at the Star Next Door by Ammitsu (Kodansha) is a sweet, heartfelt shojo romance. Chiaki Amano has loved her childhood friend Subaru Hiiragi for as long as she can remember, but now he's an actor whose fame keeps growing. She tells herself it's time to give up on him, yet because they still spend so much time together, her feelings refuse to fade. It's a lovely read for anyone who enjoys slow-burn romances and childhood friends on the edge of something more.
105: Moon Boy by Lee YoungYou (Ice Kunion) is a fantasy romance manhwa rooted in Korean folklore. Years ago, Myung-Ee Joo met a classmate whose eyes turned red under the moon, just like hers, and then he vanished from everyone's memory but her own. Now in high school, she finds him on the student council with no memory of her, and learns she is an Earth Rabbit, a descendant of the moon rabbits hunted by the Fox tribe. It's a charming pick for readers who like folklore-flavored school fantasy.
106: Arcana by So-Young Lee (Tokyopop) is a classic fantasy adventure manhwa. Inez is an orphan with the rare gift of speaking to every kind of creature, and she is told she is destined to be the chosen one. Summoned to the capital, she learns she must find and bring back the guardian dragon that keeps the kingdom's fragile peace safe from a demon race waiting in the shadows. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy chosen-one quests with gentle heroines and beautiful fantasy art.
107: Never Give Up! by Hiromu Mutou (Tokyopop) is a lighthearted shojo romantic comedy set in the modeling world. Fifteen-year-old Kiri has loved her childhood friend Tohya for years and planned to confess once she became beautiful enough. When Tohya is scouted as a model, Kiri, who has a boyish look, poses as a male model named Tatsuki so she can stay close and watch over him, and both of them end up unexpectedly famous. It's a fun pick for fans of disguise comedies and devoted heroines.
109: Hour of the Zombie by Tsukasa Saimura (Seven Seas) is a tense, unusual take on zombie horror. Akira Nikaidou is going through an ordinary school day with his friends and his crush, Kurumi, when his classmates suddenly turn into zombies. Then, strangely, the zombies stop attacking, leaving Akira and the other survivors to wonder what happens next. It's a good pick for horror readers who like slow-building dread and survival stories that don't follow the usual rules.
108: High School Girls by Towa Oshima (Comics One) is a rowdy, good-natured school comedy. Eriko and her friends Yuma and Ayano are thrilled to start high school, but sneaking a tour of their new school before the opening ceremony shows them it isn't quite what they imagined. Soon they've gathered a lively circle of new friends, from an attention-loving aspiring actress to a petite girl with very odd solutions to every problem. It's a fun pick for readers who like frank, silly slice-of-life humor.
110: I Hate You More Than Anyone! by Banri Hidaka (CMX) is a warm shojo romantic comedy. Kazuha Akiyoshi is the responsible eldest daughter of a big family and attends an all-girls high school with her best friend, Senko. During the school festival, she catches the eye of Maki Sugimoto, a hairstylist, but her growing feelings for him put a strain on her friendship, because Senko has a crush on him too. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy ensemble romances with plenty of heart.
111: Pandora Seven by Yuta Kayashima (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure with a big heart. Lia is the only humania on her island, but despite her nonhuman traits she lives happily with her mother and friends. That peace ends when humans arrive and attack the people she loves, and after she opens a mysterious box, Lia sets out alone on a quest to save them. It's a good pick for readers who like determined young heroes and quests built around a world-changing secret.
116: Platinum Garden by Maki Fujita (Tokyopop) is a shojo romance with a supernatural twist. When Kazura Enomoto's grandfather dies, he leaves her to Mizuki Magahara, the son of a wealthy family, to settle his debts. Kazura expects to work as a servant but learns she is meant to be Mizuki's fiancee instead. As she adjusts to his elite school, she begins to uncover the Magahara family's unusual secret. It's a nice fit for readers who enjoy arranged-engagement romances with a touch of mystery.
119: Reborn as a Barrier Master by Naotaro Kataoka (Seven Seas) is an isekai fantasy about making a life from nothing. Overworked 34-year-old Tamotsu Kubo wakes up in another world as a six-year-old with hidden Barrier Master skills, only to land on the auction block of a slave market. When no one bids, Marquess Basam rescues him and raises him as his personal Barrier Master under the name Linus. It's a good pick for fans of underdog isekai stories where talent grows through hard work.
120: Ultra Cute by Nami Akimoto (Tokyopop) is a bubbly shojo romantic comedy. Best friends Ami and Noa have been rivals since kindergarten, always chasing the same boys and never landing any of them. At fifteen they meet Tamon and Hiro, and for once they like different guys. The boys, though, are playing a game of their own, and a meddling ex-girlfriend and an odd teacher are ready to make things harder. It's a fun, light read for fans of high-energy school romance.
121: Unholy Blood by Lina Lim (Ize Press) is a stylish, full-color supernatural thriller. Hayan Park is a pureblood vampire who just wants a quiet life, but ever since vampire-human hybrids appeared a decade ago, the world has grown dangerous and she has to keep her nature hidden. When a professor she cares about is murdered and a police captain starts to suspect her, she may need her true powers. It's a great pick for readers who like sleek vampire stories with a mystery at the core.
122: Lights Out by Myung-Jin Lee (Tokyopop) is a high school manhwa that mixes action, comedy, and a bit of romance, from the creator of Ragnarok. Nam Gung Geon is a hot-tempered transfer student with a violent streak, but his life starts to change after he meets Min Seung-Ah, whose grandfather owns an inn called Fate. Soon he's making real friends and finding his footing at school. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy tough-guy heroes with a softer side.
123: Sakura, Saku by Io Sakisaka (Viz Media) is a gentle, bittersweet shojo romance from the creator of Ao Haru Ride and Strobe Edge. When Saku Fujigaya falls suddenly ill during her commute, a mysterious boy helps her and then disappears before she can thank him. Hoping to live up to his kindness, she makes a habit of helping any stranger in need, never losing hope of finding him again. It's a lovely pick for readers who enjoy tender first-love stories.
124: Dragons Rioting by Tsuyoshi Watanabe (Yen Press) is a wild martial arts comedy with plenty of fan service. At six, Rintaro Tachibana was diagnosed with a rare condition that could kill him if he ever gets too excited around girls, so his father trained him in the mountains for ten years. At sixteen, he enrolls at what he thinks is an all-boys school, only to find it's a former girls' school that just went coed, ruled by three fearsome female "Dragons." It's for fans of brawling, over-the-top harem comedy.
125: Multi-Mind Mayhem by Ryousen Takami (One Peace Books) is an isekai fantasy with a clever twist. Young noble Bard Cornelius of the Kingdom of Mauricia shares his body with two other souls: a Sengoku-era warlord and a modern high school student who died in a traffic accident. With the three of them pooling their skills and knowledge, Bard proves a natural at both business and battlefield strategy, though keeping everyone in agreement is another matter. It's a fun pick for readers who like strategy-minded isekai stories.
126: My Stepmother and Stepsisters Aren't Wicked by Otsuji (Seven Seas) is a sweet, funny slice-of-life story that flips the Cinderella setup. After her mother dies, Miya Nakamura learns she is her father's illegitimate child and is taken in by his family. Her new stepmother and stepsisters look intimidating, but they actually adore her and want to help her settle in. Because Miya is terribly afraid of people, though, she keeps misreading their kindness. It's a heartwarming pick for readers who love found-family comedy.
127: Call to Adventure! Defeating Dungeons with a Skill Board by Renji Kuriyama (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action story based on a prize-winning web novel. Dungeons and monsters have appeared all over the world, and clearing them has become a popular pastime. Twenty-seven-year-old Haruki Karaboshi dreams of being recognized as an adventurer, but he's easily overlooked and has no combat skills. When a dungeon appears in his own garage, he finds a skill board that helps him level up fast. It's great for fans of leveling-up adventures.
128: The Condemned Villainess Goes Back in Time by Bakufu Narayama, Ebisushi (Seven Seas) is a villainess fantasy light novel. Claudia, a duke's daughter, was tricked by her scheming half-sister and sold to a brothel, where she refused to break and rose to the top. When she dies, she wakes up at fourteen, back at her academy. Armed with hard-won street smarts, she sets out to become the ultimate villain and turn the tables on everyone who wronged her. It suits readers who like bold, calculating heroines.
129: Let's Do It Already! by Aki Kusaka (Viz Media) is a frank, funny shojo romance about a couple who aren't quite on the same page. Yuri and Keiichiro Katsuragi start dating after meeting on their walks to school. Keiichiro is the heir to a prominent political family with strict rules against physical relationships before eighteen, so he keeps Yuri at arm's length, while she feels pressure because her classmates seem to be moving faster. It's a good pick for readers who like honest, comedic takes on teen relationships.
130: Otaku Vampire's Love Bite by Julietta Suzuki (Viz Media) is a lighthearted romantic comedy from the creator of Kamisama Kiss. Hina Alucard is a vampire who drinks her blood from bags and hasn't left her house in thirty years. When her father gives her a DVD of the anime Vampire Cross, she becomes completely obsessed, and she moves from Romania to Japan to live her otaku dreams. It's a fun pick for fans of goofy supernatural comedy and anyone who's ever fallen hard for a favorite anime.
131: Isekai Tensei: Recruited to Another World by Kenichi, Shibanobancha (J-Novel Club) is an easygoing isekai fantasy adventure. After Tenma Otori dies, a god from another world offers him a second chance at life. In exchange for being reborn to help save that god's dying world, Tenma gets a fresh start along with a set of powerful cheat abilities. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy classic reincarnation stories with a capable hero and a big new world to explore.
132: Beware the Villainess! by Blue Canna, Soda Ice (Ize Press) is a full-color fantasy romantic comedy with a sharp sense of humor. A college student wakes up as Melissa Foddebrat, the villainess of a formulaic romance novel. She'd like to dodge her character's downfall and live comfortably, but she's appalled by the story's male leads, from a sleazy crown prince to an obsessive merchant. Unwilling to watch the heroine suffer, Melissa sets out to rewrite the plot without them. It's great fun for fans of genre-savvy villainess stories.
133: Glasses with a Chance of Delinquent by Naruki (Seven Seas) is a sweet, funny high school romantic comedy. Hiro Momose has had bad run-ins with delinquents before, so she picks a new high school known for having none. She joins the Support Club, whose only other member is her classmate Dan Ichikura, and after he saves her from a delinquent, she learns he used to be one himself. Hiro agrees to keep his secret, and the two grow closer. It's a charming pick for fans of gentle school romance.
134: Genju no Seiza by Matsuri Akino (Tokyopop) is a supernatural fantasy from the creator of Pet Shop of Horrors. Fuuto Kamishina is a teenager who just wants a normal life, but he turns out to be the reincarnation of the High Priest of Darashaal, a small Asian kingdom. When celestial guardians come to deal with him, they discover he really is their priest. His strong spiritual sense and knack for soothing ghosts keep pulling him into trouble. It's a good fit for readers who like moody, mystical adventures.
136: My Lovey-Dovey Wife Is a Stone Cold Killer by Donten Kosaka (Seven Seas) is a sweet, funny romantic comedy with a dangerous twist. An ordinary salaryman marries Setsuna after only a short time dating, and learns after the wedding that she works as a professional assassin. Rather than run, he decides to accept her just as she is. The series follows the newlyweds as they balance cozy married life with her very unusual job. It's a delight for readers who like affectionate couples and action-flavored comedy.
137: My Room is a Dungeon Rest Stop by Tougoku Hudou (Seven Seas) is a laid-back fantasy comedy. Toru Suzuki rents an apartment that's suspiciously cheap, and he soon finds out why: its front door opens into a classic fantasy dungeon. Toru has always wanted to explore a dungeon, but when he meets Ria, a beautiful blonde knight stranded on the other side, his new life gets more complicated than he expected. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy cozy, offbeat fantasy with a domestic twist.
138: Animal Academy by Moyamu Fujino (Tokyopop) is a cute, silly shojo comedy. Neko Fukuta begs her way into Morimori Academy, a school for animals who can shape-shift into humans. The catch is that Neko is an ordinary human, so she has to pretend to be a cat while she figures out the school's many mysteries and makes friends with its animal students. It's a lighthearted pick for younger readers and anyone who loves animal characters and school comedy.
139: Heart Gear by Tsuyoshi Takaki (Viz Media) is a heartfelt post-apocalyptic sci-fi adventure from the creator of Black Torch. Nearly 200 years after a world war wiped out humanity, a girl named Roue lives happily among the ruins with a robot she calls her uncle. When her peaceful life is threatened, she must rely on Chrome, a mysterious robot, as the two set out across the world in search of a mythical utopia. It's a great pick for fans of girl-and-robot stories with plenty of action.
140: The Great Snake's Bride by Fushiashikumo (Seven Seas) is a tender romantic fantasy with a folktale feel. Miyo, a village girl with a scar on her forehead, is offered up as a bride to a giant snake. She's certain he plans to eat her, but the great snake turns out to be surprisingly kind, and the two slowly grow close. It's a quiet, heartfelt pick for readers who enjoy monster-and-maiden romances, though it touches on some heavy themes along the way.
141: The Hero Life of a (Self-Proclaimed) Mediocre Demon! by Tamagonokimi and Shiroichi Amaui (Kodansha) is a cheerful fantasy comedy. Chrono Alkon has just turned twenty and heads to the Demon King's castle for his required year of schooling, hoping for fun and friends. Then a shocking result on his class placement test throws his plans off course. Raised in a remote village, he has no idea what counts as normal. It's a fun pick for fans of overpowered heroes who don't know their own strength.
142: Battle Club by Yuji Shiozaki (Tokyopop) is a rowdy martial arts comedy from the creator of Ikki Tousen, with plenty of fan service. Mokichi Saitou is a scrawny high school student who joins the Swan Academy wrestling club after getting beaten by Tamako Kaneda, a gifted but clumsy wrestler. The story follows their training and the club's rivalries with other schools and fighting groups. It's for readers who like brawling, goofy sports action with an older-teen sense of humor.
143: Hinowa ga Crush! by Takahiro (Yen Press) is a sweeping historical fantasy action series from the writer of Akame ga Kill!, drawn by strelka. On the island of Wakoku, civil war has raged for more than a decade, giving anyone, from fishers to illegitimate children, a chance to rise through the ranks and become a hero. Hinowa, a young woman with exceptional skills, sets out to do just that, though her plans don't go smoothly. It's a great pick for fans of battle-heavy war epics.
144: Orfina by Kitsune Tennouji (CMX) is a medieval fantasy adventure with a warm friendship at its heart. Faana Risoru is the only survivor of a hometown destroyed by the Granza military, and she happens to look almost exactly like Princess Orfina of the Kingdom of Cordia. Once the king explains their striking resemblance, the two girls become fast friends, and their fates become tied together. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy classic sword-and-sorcery with royal intrigue.
146: Planet Blood by Kim Tae-Hyung (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi action manhwa set after the end of humanity's fifth world war. Nearly half of the human race has been wiped out, and with Earth badly contaminated, the survivors have colonized the Moon and Mars, planning to return once the planet is purified. The series follows the conflicts that arise as people struggle over the future of their ruined home. It's a solid pick for readers who like gritty space-age battles and dramatic science fiction.
147: Planet Ladder by Yuri Narushima (Tokyopop) is a dreamy shojo fantasy inspired by the Japanese folktale The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter. Kaguya is a teenager who was found abandoned with no memory and raised by a Japanese foster family. Then she learns she is prophesied to save just one of nine parallel worlds, and she sets out to bring peace to a warring universe while uncovering who she really is. It's a lovely fit for readers who enjoy myth-tinged, world-hopping adventures.
145: The Reformation of the World as Overseen by a Realist Demon King by Manatsu Suzuki (Yen Press) is a strategy-minded isekai fantasy. Astaroth is reborn in an unfamiliar land as a Demon King, charged by a mysterious goddess with bringing the world under his rule and setting its disorder right. As the youngest of the Demon Kings, he has far fewer forces than his rivals, so he leans on deception and cunning to win. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy clever, pragmatic rulers outmaneuvering stronger foes.
148: There's a Demon Lord on the Floor by Masaki Kawakami (Seven Seas) is a cheerful supernatural comedy. Patricia Amon, a powerful Demon Lord, barely escapes an attack by the Clan of Light and flees to the human world to recover. To blend in, she takes a job at the Humming Dining restaurant and falls for its cooking. Now the head chef has to keep up with her enormous appetite while training her into a model employee. It's a fun, cozy read for fans of workplace comedies.
150: Thunder 3 by Yuki Ikeda (Kodansha) is a wild sci-fi action story with a playful twist. Three ordinary schoolboys get hold of a DVD said to open a gateway to a parallel universe. While their backs are turned, one boy's little sister slips through and is kidnapped by the aliens who have overrun that version of Earth. In the realistic parallel world, the boys' cartoonish bodies make them superhumanly strong, so they set out to rescue her. It's a great pick for fans of bold, inventive action.
151: Psycho Busters by Yuya Aoki (Del Rey) is a supernatural action story drawn by Akinari Nao. Kakeru is a middle schooler who wishes his dull life were more exciting, and he gets his wish when he meets a group of gifted teens, the Psychics, who are on the run from a sinister organization called the Greenhouse. Kakeru decides to help them, even though he seems to have no powers of his own. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy psychic battles and kids-on-the-run adventures.
152: Crossroad by Shioko Mizuki (Go! Comi) is a heartfelt shojo family drama. After her grandmother dies, fifteen-year-old Kajitsu moves in with her two stepbrothers and young stepsister, none of whom are related to one another. When their mother abandons six-year-old Satsuki, the three older teens are left to build a household and a family on their own. It's a moving pick for readers who enjoy found-family stories and quiet, emotional slice-of-life drama.
153: Killer Shark in Another World by Kuboken (Seven Seas) is an unhinged fantasy action parody. Shiromi Lovecut-Toothrough is considered the worst summoner in the world, until she summons Sharkiller, a creature that can transform into the fiercest sharks from Hollywood B-movies. Her new companion is bloodthirsty and eager to take down everyone in sight, and Shiromi has to decide whether she can use him to defeat the Demon King. It's perfect for readers who love over-the-top monster mayhem and gleefully silly humor.
155: Red Prowling Devil by Toshimitsu Shimizu (Comics One) is a high-flying military action manga. Naomi is a pilot who accidentally shot down a civilian airliner, and to avoid a life sentence she agrees to fly covert missions for a secret global power. Flying a red MiG-29 to earn money for a sick relative, she becomes an infamous ace known as the Red Prowling Devil, hunted by rival air forces and terrorist groups. It's a great pick for fans of fighter jets and dogfight-heavy adventure.
157: LiLing-Po by Ako Yutenji (Tokyopop) is a lively adventure with a roguish hero. LiLing-Po is a master thief who finally gets caught by the government, and the only way he can win his freedom is by recovering eight magical treasures that were recently stolen from the government. Escorted by two officials, Mei-Toku and Bu-cho, he sets off to track down the Eight Great Treasures. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy charming thieves, quest stories, and a good dose of comedy.
158: Satisfaction Guaranteed by Ryo Saenagi (Tokyopop) is a warm, offbeat comedy with a touch of mystery. Shima Yoshitsune and Kaori Suruga run Anything Inc., an all-purpose agency that takes on odd jobs, strange requests, and the occasional mystery. The two partners lean on each other in different ways: Kaori depends on Shima, and Shima finds comfort in Kaori's smile. It's a charming pick for readers who enjoy episodic case-of-the-week stories built around a close-knit duo.
159: World War Blue by Anastasia Shestakova (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action story that playfully reimagines the classic video game console wars. The Segua Kingdom and the Ninteldo Empire are locked in a war for the continent of Consume, and Segua is losing badly. Then a boy named Gear arrives, blessed with remarkable speed, and joins the Segua army to avenge his best friend, who was killed by Ninteldo soldiers. It's a fun pick for gamers who'll enjoy spotting the many nods to classic consoles and characters.
160: Love's in Sight! by Uoyama (Viz Media) is a sweet, gentle romance about seeing past first impressions. Morio Kurokawa looks like the toughest guy in town, and just about everyone is afraid of him. Yukiko Akaza, a confident girl with a visual impairment who attends a school for the blind, sees past his intimidating image to the kind person underneath, someone still figuring out his place in the world. It's a heartwarming pick for readers who enjoy tender, slow-blooming love stories.
161: Dragon Eye by Kairi Fujiyama (Del Rey) is a dark sci-fi action series. Forty years ago, a virus began turning people and animals into monsters called Dracules. In the city of Mikuni, humans immune to the virus, known as VIUS, fight back against the creatures. The story follows Squad Zero, led by Issa, a fighter with a mysterious Dragon Eye in his forehead. It's a great pick for readers who like monster-hunting squads and gritty, battle-heavy stories.
162: Dungeon Dive: Aim for the Deepest Level by Keisuke Sato (Seven Seas) is an isekai fantasy adventure based on a light novel series. Kanami Aikawa is suddenly pulled into a world of magic and monsters, where adventurers band together to clear the Dungeon, a mysterious hundred-level labyrinth. Legend says anyone who reaches the bottom will have any wish granted. Kanami just wants to get home to his ill younger sister, but first a level-one novice has to survive. It's a good fit for fans of dungeon-crawling fantasy.
163: Yubisaki Milk Tea by Tomochika Miyano (Tokyopop) is a seinen romantic comedy with a gender-bending twist. High school student Yoshinori Ikeda fills in for his sister at a modeling job and discovers that he enjoys dressing as a girl. As his alter ego, Yuki, he helps his shy classmate Minamo Kurokawa open up, all while struggling with his feelings for her and for his childhood friend, Hidari Morii. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy love triangles and stories about figuring out who you are.
165: Kurozakuro by Yoshinori Natsume (Viz Media) is a dark supernatural horror story. High school student Mikito Sakurai is bullied but refuses to fight back. Then he swallows a mysterious orb that transforms him into an ogre-like being with superhuman strength and a growing craving for violence and human flesh. Soon he's drawn into a conflict with hunters who track down ogres. It's a gripping pick for readers who like monster transformation stories and tense, bloody action.
166: The White Cat's Revenge as Plotted from the Dragon King's Lap by Kureha (J-Novel Club) is a cozy fantasy romance light novel. Ruri Morikawa is summoned to a fantasy world along with her classmates, but she's falsely accused of plotting against the priestess and abandoned in a deep forest. There she learns she is beloved by magical spirits and gains a bracelet that lets her turn into a white cat. It's a sweet pick for readers who like gentle, heartwarming fantasy.
169: St. Dragon Girl by Natsumi Matsumoto (Viz Media) is a lively shojo action romance. Momoka Sendou, nicknamed Dragon Girl, is a martial artist whose childhood friend Ryuga Kou is a magic user who battles demons. When Ryuga tries to boost his power by summoning a dragon spirit, it bonds with Momoka instead, so the two have no choice but to team up against the demons. It's a fun pick for readers who like spunky heroines, kung fu fights, and a slow-building childhood-friend romance.
170: Minecraft: The Manga by Kazuyoshi Seto (Viz Media) is a bright, kid-friendly adventure set in the world of the hit video game. Nico White, the son of a great adventurer, sets out on a journey to find the End of the World. It's a great pick for young Minecraft fans and anyone looking for an upbeat, easy-to-read adventure. Kids who love the game will enjoy seeing its blocky world turned into a classic manga quest.
171: I Tamed My Ex-Husband's Mad Dog by Jkyum, CMJM, Jagae (Ize Press) is a full-color fantasy romance with a sharp revenge plot. Grieving her father, Reinhardt Lincke finds herself sent back fifteen years to his funeral, where she stabs her betrothed, Prince Michel, whom she blames for her father's death. Banished to Luden, a cold and isolated domain, she is rescued by a wild boy who is destined to become a war hero and was once Michel's "mad dog." It's a gripping pick for fans of second-chance villainess-style dramas.
172: Sweet Blood by Se-Yeong Kim (Netcomics) is a dark fantasy BL manhwa with a vampire twist. Sooho is a teenage boy abandoned by his parents and struggling to get by in a rundown apartment. Things only get worse when an eccentric vampire king from another world takes a keen interest in his blood. To protect a classmate, Sooho offers himself up to the king's nightly visits, only to find there's no easy way out of their bond. It's a good fit for readers who like moody supernatural romance.
173: Breasts Are My Favorite Things in the World! by Wakame Konbu (Yen Press) is a cheeky yuri romantic comedy. Chiaki Ichihara is a popular high school girl with an unusual secret: nothing relaxes her quite like touching another girl's chest. Her friend Hana Harumi agrees to help her out, but Hana is quietly starting to develop real feelings for Chiaki. It's a silly, affectionate pick for readers who enjoy fan-service comedy with a sweet romance underneath.
174: Beyblade X by Homura Kawamoto (Viz Media) is a high-energy kids' battle manga, drawn by Posuka Demizu of The Promised Neverland. Bladers from all over compete to climb The X, a towering arena where only the best rise to the top. New technology and fierce rivals push every Beyblade to its limits, and every match is a fight for glory. It's a great pick for young fans of the toys and anime, and for anyone who loves fast-paced tournament action.
175: The Long Summer of August 31 by Ikkado Ito (Seven Seas) is a funny, frank seinen comedy with a time-loop twist. High schoolers Takaya Suzuki and Kana Takagi find themselves stuck reliving August 31st over and over, and the loop has been going for a month. Suzuki suspects the whole thing may be tied to his own wish to get a girlfriend before summer ends. It's a good pick for older readers who enjoy awkward, honest teen comedy and sci-fi setups with a romantic heart.
176: Infini-T Force by Ukyo Kodachi & Tatsuma Ejiri (Nakama Press) is a superhero action manga that brings together Tatsunoko's classic heroes. High school student Emi Kaido receives a mysterious pencil that can grant wishes. When her life is threatened, she uses it to summon legendary heroes including Gatchaman, Tekkaman, Casshan, and Polymar, who cross space and time to protect her. It's a treat for longtime fans of these characters and for anyone who loves big team-up adventures.
177: Witch and Mercenary by Chohokiteki Kaeru (Seven Seas) is a grounded fantasy light novel. On the Old Continent, witches are feared and hunted. Mercenary Zig Crane joins a witch hunt and fights the witch Saoirse to a standstill, and the two find common ground as people forced into killing by the world around them. Saoirse hires Zig to escort her to the New Continent, where magic is commonplace, only to find that its peaceful society shuns mercenaries instead. It's great for fans of slow-burn partnerships.
179: The Barbarian's Bride by Noriaki Kotoba (Seven Seas) is a fantasy romantic comedy with plenty of sword-swinging action. Serafina de Lavillant, the strongest knight in the West, is captured in a war against the barbarians of the East and handed over to their king, Veor, as his bride. To her surprise, Veor is handsome and refined and sets out to win her over, while Serafina is focused on plotting her escape. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy fierce heroines and enemies-to-lovers banter.
180: Ako and Bambi by Hero (Yen Press) is a gentle supernatural comedy from the creator of Horimiya. Bambi is a struggling amateur novelist who moves into a cheap apartment, only to discover it's haunted. The ghost isn't hostile; she's lost her memories and needs somewhere to stay until she can move on. Since Bambi needs material for his writing, the two strike a deal that works for both of them. It's a cozy, quietly funny pick for fans of odd-couple stories.
182: Tsumiki Ogami's Not-So-Ordinary Life by Miyu Morishita (Viz Media) is a warm, funny school romance with a supernatural twist. Yutaka Shinso worries constantly about how other people see him. When he transfers to a new high school where vampires, ogres, and other supernatural beings attend class alongside everyone else, he finds himself drawn to Tsumiki Ogami, a confident, popular werewolf girl. It's a sweet pick for readers who enjoy gentle romantic comedies and lovable monster characters.
183: The Ayakashi Hunter's Tainted Bride by Mamenosuke Fujimaru (Kodansha) is a dark historical fantasy romance. Nanao Byakurenji has unusually strong spiritual energy, but after an ayakashi leaves a mark on her forehead, her village treats her as cursed. Yako Benitsubaki, an official who hunts yokai, needs the blood of women with strong spiritual energy to survive, and he rescues Nanao with an offer of a contract marriage. It's a lovely pick for fans of slow-burn arranged-marriage romances with a supernatural edge.
185: 12 Beast by Okayado (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action comedy from the creator of Monster Musume. High schooler Eita Touga is a video game fan and the heir to a ninja dojo. He's pulled into a fantasy world called Re-Verse by Aero, a winged harpy girl, and agrees to help defend the harpies from giant robotic monsters called Gigas while searching for his missing brother. It's a good fit for readers who like monster-girl comedy mixed with ninja action and plenty of fan service.
186: A Reincarnated Witch Spells Doom by Tail Yuzuhara and Sora (Yen Press) is a gentle fantasy romance. Reclusive Sena Shirai finally decides to step outside on her eighteenth birthday, only to be struck by a truck. She's reborn as a witch in another world, but her only magic is destructive, and her powers frighten the nearby villagers until she's isolated all over again. Then, on her second eighteenth birthday, a mysterious boy collapses at her door. It's a sweet pick for readers who like lonely heroines.
187: Forget Me Not by Nao Emoto (Kodansha) is a bittersweet romance drama, written by Mag Hsu. After a scooter accident, Yusuke Serizawa wakes up in a hospital bed. A familiar face distracted him just before the crash, and that same woman called the ambulance but won't say who she is. All Yusuke knows is that she's someone from his past, someone he loved and may have wronged, so he searches his memories of past loves to find her. It's a thoughtful pick for fans of grown-up love stories.
188: Model by Lee So-Young (Tokyopop) is a moody, romantic vampire manhwa from the creator of Arcana. A Korean art student studying in Europe reluctantly lets a drunk stranger crash at her apartment after a friend brings him over. That night, she dreams that he drank her blood. In the morning she finds him striking and offers to draw him as payment, and once she mentions the dream, he agrees to sit for her in exchange for her blood. It's a good pick for readers who like gothic, slow-burning romance.
189: Gatcha Gacha by Yutaka Tachibana (Tokyopop) is a shojo school drama with a romantic streak. High schooler Yuri Muroi has a reputation among the boys and a rough time fitting in, but she's drawn into friendships with playboy Takahiro Yabe, the popular Motoko Kagurazaka, and student body president Sho Hirao. As she gets closer to them, she starts to uncover a painful past that ties the group together. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy emotional friend-group stories with a hint of mystery.
191: Tena on S-String by Sesuna Mikabe (Yen Press) is a supernatural fantasy with a musical twist. After a car accident nearly kills him, Kyosuke Hibiki gains the ability to see and hear the Soul Score, a mysterious musical record of every person's life. He soon meets Tena, a tuner who can play the score and remove its discordant notes. Tena wants Kyosuke as her pet, but he isn't about to go along with it. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy offbeat fantasy and prickly partnerships.
192: Go Go Heaven!! by Keiko Yamada (CMX) is a quirky shojo comedy with a supernatural heart. Shirayuki is bullied and unhappy at school, and then she dies in a car accident on the very first day of a new Prince of Hell's job. Smitten with her, the Prince gives her 49 days to return to her life and settle her unfinished business, while he and three subordinates keep watch from a dollhouse in her bedroom. It's a fun pick for readers who like afterlife comedies with a sweet side.
194: Ani-Imo by Haruko Kurumatani (Yen Press) is a body-swap romantic comedy. Youta and his sister Hikaru were raised as twins, but they aren't actually related by blood. When an accident causes them to switch bodies, Hikaru, now in Youta's body, confesses that she has loved him romantically for years and is determined to win him over. It's a playful pick for readers who enjoy body-swap shenanigans and unconventional shojo romance.
195: Archlord by Jin-Hwan Park (Tokyopop) is a classic sword-and-sorcery manhwa connected to the online game of the same name. It tells the story of a young hero who must grow up and learn to harness the power of a magical sword so he can restore balance to his land and fulfill his destiny as the Archlord. It's a solid pick for readers who enjoy chosen-hero quests, big fantasy battles, and coming-of-age adventure.
196: The Fiancee Chosen by the Ring by Jyun Hayase (Yen Press) is a charming fantasy romance. Aurora el la Porta is a noblewoman whose true passion is embroidery, and she mainly attends lavish evening parties to collect ideas for her designs. One night a mysterious wedding ring flies across the room and strikes her, and when she picks it up, one of the kingdom's top knights claims her as his fiancee. It's a sweet pick for readers who enjoy cozy historical romances with a crafty heroine.
197: The First Night with the Duke by Hwang DoTol (Net Comics) is a full-color fantasy romantic comedy based on a web novel. A college student wakes up inside her favorite romance novel as Ripley, a minor side character. She plans to enjoy her new status and watch the story unfold from the sidelines, but she ends up spending a night with Duke Zeronis, the novel's hero. Now she has to dodge the villainess, the duke's advances, and her own feelings. It's a fun pick for fans of genre-savvy isekai romance.
198: Now by Park Sung Woo (Comics One) is a martial arts action manhwa set in the ancient Korean kingdom of Goguryeo. It follows Bi-Ryu, a skilled martial artist, and Ah-Rin, a cheerful girl who wields a sword, as they set off on a string of adventures and run into rival fighters along the way. It's a great pick for readers who enjoy fast, flowing fight scenes and classic wuxia-style adventure.
199: Beauty is the Beast by Tomo Matsumoto (Viz Media) is a lighthearted shojo romantic comedy. Bubbly eleventh-grader Eimi moves into the dormitory at Seikei Academy, and before long she's caught up in the romantic ups and downs of her new dorm-mates, along with a budding connection of her own with Wanibuchi. The story plays out as a collection of offbeat love stories. It's a fun pick for readers who like quirky ensemble casts and dorm-life comedy.
112: The Testament of Sister New Devil by Tetsuto Uesu (Seven Seas) is an action-packed supernatural romantic comedy with plenty of fan service. High schooler Basara Toujou's father announces that he's remarrying and promptly leaves the country, so Basara is suddenly living with two new stepsisters, Mio and Maria. He soon learns the girls are not what they seem: Mio is the heir to a demon lord, and Maria is a succubus. It's for older teen readers who enjoy ecchi harem comedy with real battles.
117: Plus-Sized Elf by Synecdoche (Seven Seas) is a silly fantasy comedy with plenty of fan service. Naoe is a bodywork therapist who meets Elfuda, an elf who crossed over to Japan and has put on a lot of weight from snacking on human junk food. Determined to help her slim down, Naoe puts her on a diet and exercise plan, and soon other fantasy women with the same problem come looking for help. It's for older readers who enjoy cheeky, good-natured comedy.
118: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon by Andy Seto (Comics One) is a sweeping wuxia action epic in Hong Kong manhua style. It adapts Wang Du Lu's classic martial arts novels, the same source that inspired the famous film, following swordsman Li Mu Bai and the warriors, rivals, and lovers whose lives become entwined with his. Expect dramatic duels, codes of honor, and richly painted artwork. It's a great pick for fans of martial arts cinema and historical adventure.
135: Alice in the Country of Joker: Circus and Liar's Game by QuinRose (Seven Seas) is a romantic fantasy adventure based on the popular otome game series. Alice Liddell has settled into life in a strange Wonderland full of charming, dangerous residents. Then the season changes, and a mysterious circus led by the enigmatic Joker arrives, bringing new games and new secrets with it. It's a lovely pick for readers who enjoy dreamy, offbeat takes on Alice in Wonderland with plenty of romance.
156: Lagoon Engine by Yukiru Sugisaki (Tokyopop) is a supernatural action comedy from the creator of D.N.Angel. Brothers Yen and Jin Ragun come from a long line of ghost hunters, and they take on troublesome spirits by uncovering their true names. Balancing schoolwork, sibling squabbles, and the family business keeps the two boys very busy. It's a fun pick for readers who like spooky monster-of-the-week adventures with a light touch and beautiful art.
164: Durarara!! Re;Dollars Arc by Ryohgo Narita (Yen Press) is an urban supernatural drama set in Tokyo's Ikebukuro. Picking up after the earlier Durarara!! arcs, it follows the neighborhood's sprawling cast of oddballs, informants, gangs, and a headless rider as new faces arrive and the mysterious online group known as the Dollars begins to change. It's a great pick for readers who already love the series and enjoy big ensemble casts where everyone has a secret.
178: A Star Brighter than the Sun by Kazune Kawahara (Viz Media) is a sweet shojo romantic comedy from the writer of My Love Story!! Sae Iwata has had a crush on her childhood friend Kohei Kamiya since elementary school, back when she was the taller of the two. Now in high school, Kohei has grown tall and popular, and Sae worries she doesn't stand a chance with him. It's a warm, funny pick for readers who enjoy earnest heroines and childhood-friend romances.
190: Alice in the Country of Clover: Cheshire Cat Waltz by QuinRose (Seven Seas) is a romantic fantasy based on the popular otome game series. Alice Liddell is living in a topsy-turvy Wonderland where many of the residents are handsome and dangerous. In this story, she grows close to Boris Airay, the playful and mischievous Cheshire Cat, and their friendship slowly turns into something more. It's a charming pick for readers who enjoy whimsical Alice retellings with a sweet romance at the center.
193: Angels of Death Episode 0 by Kudan Naduka (Yen Press) is a dark horror thriller and a side story to the Angels of Death manga. It turns the spotlight on Danny, one of the series' most unsettling figures, and reveals the mysteries of his past. Before he came to work at a prison, a meeting with a priest changed his life forever. It's a gripping pick for fans of the series and readers who like tense, psychological horror.
